verses.saheeh: May the hands of Abu Lahab be ruined, and ruined is he.
verses.khattab: May the hands of Abu Lahab perish, and he ˹himself˺ perish
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Perish, ruined be, the hands of Abū Lahab, in other words, all of him — the use of ‘hands’ here to denote [all of] him is figurative, and is because most actions are performed by them; the statement is an invocation — and perish he!, may he be ruined! (this [tabba] is a predicate, as where one says, ahlakahu’Llāhu wa-qad halak, ‘God destroyed him and he indeed is destroyed’. When the Prophet threatened him with the chastisement, he said, ‘If what my brother’s son says is true, then I shall ransom [myself] from it with my wealth and sons!’; so the following was revealed:
verses.romanUrdu: Toot gaye Abu Lahab ke haath aur na-murad ho gaya woh

verses.uthmani: مَآ أَغۡنَىٰ عَنۡهُ مَالُهُۥ وَمَا كَسَبَ
verses.indopak: مَاۤ اَغْنٰى عَنْهُ مَالُهٗ وَمَا كَسَبَ ۗ
verses.saheeh: His wealth will not avail him or that which he gained.
verses.khattab: Neither his wealth nor ˹worldly˺ gains will benefit him
verses.jalalayn: ﻿His wealth will not avail him, nor what he has earned (wa-kasab means wa-kasbihi, that is to say, his sons; mā aghnā means [mā] yughnī).
verses.romanUrdu: Uska maal aur jo kuch us ne kamaya woh uske kisi kaam na aaya

verses.saheeh: He will [enter to] burn in a Fire of [blazing] flame
verses.khattab: He will burn in a flaming Fire
verses.jalalayn: ﻿He will [soon] enter a Fire of flames, that is to say, [a fire that is] flaming and ignited (this [statement] is the source of his nickname, [which was given to him] on account of his flaming reddish fair face),
verses.romanUrdu: Zaroor woh shola zan Aag mei dala jayega

verses.saheeh: And his wife [as well] - the carrier of firewood.
verses.khattab: and ˹so will˺ his wife, the carrier of ˹thorny˺ kindling
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and his wife (wa’mra’atuhu is a supplement to the person [of the verb] yaslā, ‘he will enter’, separated by the clause of the direct object and its qualification) — and this was Umm Jamīl — the carrier (read hammālatu or hammālata) of firewood, cactus and thorns which she used to fling into the path of the Prophet (s).
verses.romanUrdu: Aur (us ke saath) us ki joru(wife) bhi lagai bujhai karne wali

verses.saheeh: Around her neck is a rope of [twisted] fiber.
verses.khattab: around her neck will be a rope of palm-fibre
verses.jalalayn: ﻿with a rope of palm-fibre around her neck (fī jīdihā hablun min masadin is a circumstantial qualifier referring to hammālata’l-hatab, which in turn is [either] a description of imra’atahu, ‘his wife’, or the predicate of an implied subject).
verses.romanUrdu: Us ki gardan(neck) mein moonj ki rassi hogi
